diagnostic_evidence.quote:
Once $k=\tilde n$, $\Q_k$ contains a null vector of $\A$, 
which can be scaled arbitrarily large to yield an arbitrarily small backward error.
We note that inverse iteration would then break down in exact arithmetic

issues.failure_explanation: For example, if nonzero $\b\in\ker(\A)$, then every nonzero Krylov vector is $\x=t\b$ and its backward error is $1/(\|\A\|_2|t|)$, whose infimum is zero but which has no finite minimizer. Thus the argmin defining $\x_k$ does not exist in an allowed PSD case. The source itself acknowledges the unbounded scaling and exact-arithmetic breakdown.

failure_location.quote: For any $n\times n$ PSD matrix $\A$, vector $\b\in\R^n$ and $k \ge 2$, the MINBERR iterate sequence \eqref{eq:minberr} satisfies:

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the source's suggested regularization $\A+\epsilon\|\A\|_2\I$, together with the composition lemma, and supply the resulting convergence and complexity argument for singular PSD inputs; alternatively restrict the results and algorithm to positive-definite matrices.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed MINBERR iterate sequence is undefined on part of the advertised singular-PSD regime, and the corollary's PSD-wide algorithmic guarantee does not follow from the positive-definite complexity theorem.
issues.title: MINBERR minimizer need not exist for singular PSD systems
issues.why_classification: Preserving the advertised singular-PSD scope requires modifying the construction and adding a contained regularization argument; merely editing notation does not make the stated argmin exist.

issues.failure_explanation: The transformed finite eigenvector is $[\alpha;\v_{\min}]$. Scaling its first coordinate to the required value $-1$ gives $[-1;-\v_{\min}/\alpha]$, so the coefficient vector is $-\v_{\min}/\alpha$, not $\v_{\min}/\alpha$. For the scalar system $A=b=1$, the stated formula returns $x=-1$ instead of the exact solution $x=1$. The same sign error appears in both algorithms and in the normal-equations proposition.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace every reconstruction $\Q_k\v/\alpha$ by $-\Q_k\v/\alpha$ and make the corresponding sign correction throughout the two proofs and algorithms.
issues.overall_effect: As written, both executable algorithms generally return the negative of the intended minimizer, invalidating their backward-error output guarantees and the downstream complexity guarantee.
issues.title: The reconstructed MINBERR solution has the wrong sign
issues.why_classification: A uniform local sign correction restores the intended minimizer without changing the method, convergence rate, complexity, or scope.

issues.failure_explanation: The generalized Rayleigh quotient and the reduced singular value equal $\|A x-b\|_2/\|x\|_2$. By the paper's own definition, relative backward error is this quantity divided by $\|A\|_2$. Hence the correct identity is $\berr_{A,b}(x_k)=\sigma_{\min}/\|A\|_2$. The algorithms likewise compare $\sigma_{\min}$ directly with the dimensionless tolerance $\epsilon$, so their stopping tests are not invariant under scaling $A$ and $b$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Normalize $A$ and $b$ before the reductions, or divide all reported singular values by $\|A\|_2$ and test against $\epsilon\|A\|_2$.
issues.overall_effect: The singular-value identities and both tolerance-based stopping guarantees are false unless $\|A\|_2=1$; rescaling an equivalent linear system can change when the algorithms stop.
issues.title: Implementation confuses residual quotient with relative backward error
issues.why_classification: A standard scaling correction preserves the minimizers, rates, and asymptotic complexity and requires no new mathematical argument.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: In particular, for a $1/2$-relative error ($\Delta = 0.5$), we require $\ell \geq 2.23 \ln(n/\delta^2)$.

issues.failure_explanation: Substituting $\Delta=1/2$ into the proved lemma gives $\frac12[1+\ln(64n\ln(2/\delta)/(\pi\delta^2))/\ln(1.25)]$. This is not bounded by $2.23\ln(n/\delta^2)$ as claimed: even the leading coefficient $1/(2\ln 1.25)$ is about $2.2407>2.23$, and the omitted additive constant and $\ln\ln(2/\delta)$ term further increase the requirement. Thus the algorithm's iteration count does not establish its stated success probability.

failure_location.quote:
Applying Lemma \ref{lemma:invit} to $\tilde \T^\top\tilde\T$ shows that $\ell \geq 2.23 \ln(k / \delta^2)$
 steps of inverse iteration suffice to get $\Delta=1/2$ relative accuracy with probability at least $1-\delta$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use the explicit iteration bound from Lemma \ref{lemma:invit}, or a valid larger simplified bound including its constants and logarithmic terms; this leaves the asymptotic complexity unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The high-probability approximation and complexity guarantees are unsupported for the exact inverse-iteration count used by the algorithms.
issues.title: The stated inverse-iteration count does not follow from the proved bound
issues.why_classification: Increasing the inverse-iteration count by a local constant/additive-log correction restores the probability guarantee without changing the algorithmic rate or advertised asymptotic complexity.
